newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe cutting army to about 30,000 from 40,000.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe cutting army to about 30,000 from 40,000.

text.p: Zimbabwe has recently reduced its army by 5,000 soldiers and plans to cut a similar number in coming months to around 30,000, Defence Minister Moven Mahachi told the state-controlled Herald newspaper on Tuesday.

He said the cuts were aimed at helping President Robert Mugabe's government reduce spending, accounting for about 38 percent of gross domestic product, and transforming the army into a defensive rather than offensive organisation.
"Apart from retrenchment we want to allow retirement and natural wastage to help us reduce the army," Mahachi said.
In the last seven years, Zimbabwe's cash-strapped government had cut the army to 40,000 from 50,000.
